messages.subject: Dealing with zero.cell.tables - binary data
parts:
Hello everyone,
I am working on my first SEM project and I am performing a CFA for a test consisting of 42 items which are scored with 0 points for a false answer and 1 point for a correct answer. I am performing this CFA as a part of a validation of a translation, testing whether the same factor structure can be obtained in the translated test version .

When performing the analysis with the following code:

   STEU_modell <- 'f1 =~ 1* v1_s+v5_s+v7_s+v10_s+v14_s+v22_s+v25_s+v30_s+v32_s+v36_s+v37_s+v39_s+v24_s+v31_s #nocontext
           f2 =~ 1* v2_s+v6_s+v8_s+v11_s+v13_s+v15_s+v18_s+v20_s+v21_s+v23_s+v34_s+v38_s+v41_s+v33_s #work
           f3 =~ 1* v3_s+v4_s+v9_s+v12_s+v16_s+v17_s+v19_s+v26_s+v27_s+v28_s+v29_s+v35_s+v40_s+v42_s' #personal

STEU_fit.modell <- cfa(STEU_modell, data=daten,std.lv=T)
summary(STEU_fit.modell, fit.measures=TRUE)

I get the following output: 

> test_modell <- 'f1 =~ 1* v1_s+v5_s+v7_s+v10_s+v14_s+v22_s+v25_s+v30_s+v32_s+v36_s+v37_s+v39_s+v24_s+v31_s 
+            f2 =~ 1* v2_s+v6_s+v8_s+v11_s+v13_s+v15_s+v18_s+v20_s+v21_s+v23_s+v34_s+v38_s+v41_s+v33_s 
+            f3 =~ 1* v3_s+v4_s+v9_s+v12_s+v16_s+v17_s+v19_s+v26_s+v27_s+v28_s+v29_s+v35_s+v40_s+v42_s' 
> 
> test_fit.modell <- cfa(test_modell, data=daten,std.lv=T)
Warning message:
In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :
  lavaan WARNING: 27 bivariate tables have empty cells; to see them, use:
                  lavInspect(fit, "zero.cell.tables")
> summary(STEU_fit.modell, fit.measures=TRUE)
lavaan (0.5-23.1097) converged normally after  23 iterations


Since I am pretty new to SEM I now have the following questions/ am unsure which path to follow:
How do I deal with those empty cells in the bivariate tables?

Using: 
lavInspect() I identified that the empty cells were caused by only 3 variables. Would it be suitable to just exclude the three variables? If yes, why?


Then I stumbled about: Savalaei's paper: "What to Do About Zero Frequency Cells When Estimating Polychoric Correlations" who recommends using the ADD method for binary data. Would that be a more suitable approach? If yes: What are lavaans defaults for DWLS calculation and how do I select the ADD method to replace the empty cells?

 

Best wishes,

Eric

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Dealing with zero.cell.tables - binary data
parts:
Since I am pretty new to SEM I now have the following questions/ am unsure which path to follow:
How do I deal with those empty cells in the bivariate tables?
If everything ran ok (no convergence issues, no large standard errors), then most likely, everything is fine.

> lavInspect() I identified that the empty cells were caused by only 3
variables.
That is why you got a warning, so you would inspect your data. Now you know which variables are involved, and this may or may not be informative for you.
Would it be suitable to just exclude the three variables?

No.

Then I stumbled about: Savalaei's paper: "What to Do About Zero Frequency Cells When Estimating Polychoric Correlations"<http://www.tandfonline.com/author/Savalei%2C+Victoria>who recommends using the ADD method for binary data.

By default, lavaan implements exactly the methods advocated in this paper. Type in R:

?lavOptions,

and in the subsection 'Categorical estimation options:', you can read:


 'zero.add': A numeric vector containing two values. These values
          affect the calculation of polychoric correlations when some
          frequencies in the bivariate table are zero. The first value
          only applies for 2x2 tables. The second value for larger
          tables. This value is added to the zero frequency in the
          bivariate table. If '"default"', the value is set depending
          on the '"mimic"' option. By default, lavaan uses 'zero.add =
          c(0.5. 0.0)'.

     'zero.keep.margins': Logical. This argument only affects the
          computation of polychoric correlations for 2x2 tables with an
          empty cell, and where a value is added to the empty cell. If
          'TRUE', the other values of the frequency table are adjusted
          so that all margins are unaffected. If '"default"', the value
          is set depending on the '"mimic"'. The default is 'TRUE'.

     'zero.cell.warn': Logical. Only used if some observed endogenous
          variables are categorical. If 'TRUE', give a warning if one
          or more cells of a bivariate frequency table are empty.



Yves.
